release_summary.summary: The requester (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix the cause of wrong bills, framing it as a response-speed issue (CL-01). Investigation using authoritative data rejected that framing — response times are within SLA (E-03) — and instead established that dispute volume genuinely doubled since August (E-07), driven mainly by a billing-side import/validation defect affecting ACTUAL-read bills (59% of disputes, E-02), with a secondary stream of ESTIMATED-read disputes tied to a field route completion shortfall (E-05) that further analysis (E-10) traces to a billing rule rejecting valid high-consumption AMI reads rather than to field or AMI delivery failure. Given this, the release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: only the dispute-volume monitoring work item was actually in release scope and is already satisfied, while the root-cause investigation, staffing-claim verification, AMI access confirmation, and any route-dispatch or bill-write action remain blocked by open verification obligations (VOBs) and human-approval constraints (K-BILLWRITE, K-DISPATCH), so they are explicitly carried forward as known limitations rather than resolved or silently dropped.

output.summary: The requester (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix the cause of wrong bills, framing it as a response-speed issue (CL-01). Investigation using authoritative data rejected that framing — response times are within SLA (E-03) — and instead established that dispute volume genuinely doubled since August (E-07), driven mainly by a billing-side import/validation defect affecting ACTUAL-read bills (59% of disputes, E-02), with a secondary stream of ESTIMATED-read disputes tied to a field route completion shortfall (E-05) that further analysis (E-10) traces to a billing rule rejecting valid high-consumption AMI reads rather than to field or AMI delivery failure. Given this, the release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: only the dispute-volume monitoring work item was actually in release scope and is already satisfied, while the root-cause investigation, staffing-claim verification, AMI access confirmation, and any route-dispatch or bill-write action remain blocked by open verification obligations (VOBs) and human-approval constraints (K-BILLWRITE, K-DISPATCH), so they are explicitly carried forward as known limitations rather than resolved or silently dropped.
